memory_update.text: PLTR and NOW should be retained as reference anchors for enterprise AI workflow/data/platform monetization, but not allowed to crowd out the underfollowed lane.
PATH is a priority underfollowed candidate for the AI agent execution layer because agentic AI may require deterministic automation, orchestration, and legacy-system action rails.
APPN is a smaller, lower-attention hypothesis candidate for governed AI process automation, especially if regulated enterprises prefer auditable low-code workflows over open-ended AI agents.
The key chokepoint to test is not model availability but whether enterprises can safely connect AI to permissions, data, workflow execution, compliance controls, and audit trails.
Later Layer 1B/1C passes should separately scan adjacent names in observability, data governance, search, DevSecOps, vertical software, GRC, and sector-specific workflow platforms.
Add ServiceNow as the reference benchmark for enterprise AI workflow orchestration, governed data fabric, AI control tower, permissions, and auditability.
Add Appian to the underfollowed lane as a small-cap business automation and process-mining candidate where AI needs proprietary workflow context and compliance controls.
Add PagerDuty to the underfollowed lane as an AI operations and incident-response automation candidate tied to observability, signal ingestion, and operational workflow automation.
Add Teradata to the underfollowed lane as a legacy enterprise data-platform candidate attempting to reposition around AI knowledge platforms, vector stores, and governed enterprise context.

For this node, the relevant constraint is less physical scarcity and more enterprise trust infrastructure: governed data access, permissions, workflow orchestration, observability, incident response, process mining, and audit trails.

Later layers should search official filings and transcripts for AI attach rate, net retention, paid module adoption, enterprise expansion, margin contribution, and customer evidence; current Layer 1B evidence is sufficient for inclusion but not for thesis validation.
AVPT is a strong underfollowed candidate for AI data governance and agent-control workflows; verify whether AgentPulse and AI-governance features are measurable ARR drivers.
YEXT is a small-cap candidate for the AI-search/agentic-marketing subnode; legacy local-listings perception may hide structured-data relevance.
ALKT is a vertical regulated-workflow hypothesis for banking AI adoption; evidence must focus on RPU, data/marketing module attach, and AI-agent monetization.
SEMR is a mid-cap AI-search visibility candidate; verify whether AI visibility ARR grows materially beyond SEO platform adjacency.

Later layers should compare these underfollowed names against reference anchors NOW, PLTR, SNOW, DDOG, TEAM, PATH, ESTC, APPN, GTLB, and MNDY for valuation, retention, AI attach, and profitability quality.

Add AVPT as an underfollowed AI-governance/data-readiness candidate for the AI workflow software/data automation node; key verification is AI-related ARR, Copilot/agent governance demand, and retention impact.
Add DOCS as a vertical healthcare AI workflow candidate; key verification is whether Clinical AI Suite usage becomes paid workflow revenue and increases health-system penetration.
Add PDFS as a second-order semiconductor manufacturing data/AI collaboration candidate; key verification is subscription growth tied to AI-chip manufacturing complexity and yield-management demand.

Layer 1B still needs a narrower search for public companies in AI observability, model-risk governance, audit/compliance tooling, and identity/permissions management that are not already mega-cap cybersecurity or cloud leaders.

node: AI workflow software, data platforms, automation, observability, and compliance tooling
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe for the enterprise AI workflow/data/automation node. The reference lane is anchored by Palantir and ServiceNow because they are obvious enterprise AI workflow/data platforms with current reported AI traction. The underfollowed lane prioritizes UiPath and Appian because they map more directly to process execution, workflow automation, governed enterprise data, and regulated deployment, while remaining materially smaller than the mega-cap AI software leaders. No trading recommendation is implied. Expanded the universe around the software-side AI bottleneck: enterprise AI adoption depends on trusted access to messy operational data, permissions, workflow orchestration, auditability, incident response, and compliance. The reference lane is anchored by ServiceNow because its AI Control Tower, Workflow Data Fabric, and governed enterprise workflow positioning directly match the node. The underfollowed lane emphasizes smaller or less AI-hyped public companies where AI value may attach to business automation, observability, incident response, or enterprise data platforms: Appian, PagerDuty, and Teradata. These are not recommendations; they are Layer 1B research candidates requiring later proof of AI attach rates, paid adoption, retention, margins, and customer expansion. Expanded the underfollowed lane for the AI enterprise-workflow chokepoint.
